CRUNCH TIME IN MADIBENG

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
ESKOM has threatened 8 hours of blackouts to those municipalities that dont pay it. Madibeng is one of them, but where did the money go

Summary:
Still to come

Further information:
A month ago Chief Financial officer of Madibeng municipality, Tondy Nkuna stood up and said ENOUGH and promptly resigned. Her letter to the Municipal manager explains that since March 2014 she has been under stress and the municipality failed to attend to her problems.

Tondy’s stress comes from pressure to sign off contracts she knows are not kosher, and unable to sustain the pressure, she has resigned.

Madibeng is one of 24 NW municipalities that for the last eight years at least, cant get the basics right. Clean audits, clean water, functioning sewerage are rare commodities here.

WATER
Last month another shortage of water across Madibeng was the final straw. In bloody and violent clashes people died on the streets. In Jericho the people who once had running water had none for ten years thanks to Madibeng.

But millions have been budgeted over the years to sort out the water problems. So what happened? Why is it that the only way that people who once had piped water now had to rely on water trucks – costing the council over a million rand a month and going into the pockets of contractors giving kickbacks to well placed politicians

This is the land of the burst water pipe. For the last three days one of Hartebeespoort suburbs is once again without water. People are so fed up they arrived with posters at a budget meeting demanding the pipes be fixed.

The Sewerage situation is no different. An insider says told Carte Blanche they don’t have money for grease or pumps. He has listed about 28 pumps that are desperately needed here. In the meantime the council pumps raw sewerage into the crocodile River and abstracts source water for drinking water a couple of hundred meters downstream. If that is not enough the abbatoir releases blood into the sewers that run into a stream that runs into the Crocodile River. The leather tanning factory uses chrome to clean its leather and that too makes its way into Brits drinking water. Councillors say the water is fine to drink but receipts show just how much they spend on bottled water, and cold drinks.

And there are thousands of rands spent on VIP toilets – but the chemicals are so strong says one angry resident they burn our butts. At the budget meeting he warned that “ you councilors who steal the money – we will hunt you down.
People are angry. Its crunch time here

Yet go through the figures, the asset registers and a picture emerges of ANC councilors spending fortunes on events, parties, transport, cars…
Below are a few of the items
Two telephone poles – worth about R3000 max – paid over a R1 million rand
R948 000 rand for the new mayors car
R45 000 a month lease for the previous mayors car
R6000 for the previous mayors chocolate cake
And hundreds of thousands on VIP toilets, catering, PA systems and events

Everyone knows who is behind the theft but few have proof and those that do have given up trying to catch them. At least nine years of investigations mysteriously go nowhere as criminal charges seem to disappear in a whiff of smoke.

Mr Cash, the former Municipal manager has built his empire in the municipality, says a source and entrenched it in waste management. Mr Cash AKA Philemon Mapulane was suspended in 2009 on charges of fraud and corruption. He was arrested but all charges against him were withdrawn. He is currently building his fourth or fifth home- at a cool R11 million, not bad for a man who started off as a meter reader. When he was suspended for corruption in Madibeng, he was promoted to treasurer in the North West Province. Now he sits on the NEC of the ANC and is a member of parliament.

Two weeks ago there were more suspensions by the current municipal manager Mr Mondi Juta. Why he is back is anyone’s guess because a 2013 report recommended criminal charges against him too.

LETS STOP THE CROOKS IN THE MUNICIPALITY
These were the words of DA councilor Eddie Barlow this morning who told a portfolio committee that they need an administrator in every department as the only way to stop the rot. The portfolio committee will write a report and submit it to the minister who has 14 days to decide what to do.

With over a billion rand in debt Madibeng is effectively bankrupt – and they spend more than their current revenue. They are hoping to meet Eskom on the 3rd May and come to an arrangement where they can pay R50 million and the other R20 million in tranches. MORE TO COME

Press Release:


Dying for water in Madibeng
The party is over in Madibeng. For years, ‘tenderpreneurs’ have drained the coffers with large, overpriced infrastructure projects - some are missing, others don’t work. Now the municipality is a billion rand in debt, with assets worth R1.5-bn missing, and they're struggling to pay Eskom and their water bills. According to reports, looting continues. The premier says they are working hard to turn around North West’s failing municipalities, but residents have grown impatient, with angry protests over water having led to several deaths. Carte Blanche goes in search of answers.


Script:


DYING FOR WATER FINAL SCRIPT 22 May 2015

Commentary One
Last year, not far from Marikana – four people were shot dead by police.

Gunshots

Their crime, protesting about a lack of water

GUNSHOTS

This year, further water protests erupted across the North West’s Madibeng Municipality.

A water affairs investigation into what happened found that there could be 100 water supply systems like Madibeng where the management has deteriorated to such an extent a water crisis could happen any day.

Sammy Matubela
I spend about R800 a month on water

Commentary two
Here clean water costs a fortune. Pensioners can no longer afford a basic human right

Fransina
Die helfte van my pensionare geld hou ek apart vir water

Commentary Three
15 years ago Madibeng merged Hartbeespoort, Brits and the surrounding townships. Almost from the outset overpriced multimillion rand tenders were awarded. Former resident, attorney Josjeph Moyo, owns this run down bakery there. He alleges corrupt councilors still get huge kickbacks.

Josjeph Moyo
They want to enrich themselves but they forgot the poor people on ground.

Commentary four
By 2007 an investigation was handed to the Scorpions detailing 26 cases of corruption. Nothing happened.


LINK
There were others, one of those is sitting on the Presidents desk six years after it was commissioned.

Commentary Five
Now Madibeng is bankrupt. They struggle to pay water and electricity and residents both rich and poor, are venting their anger at the current budget meetings underway.

Dominique
We will hunt you down because you are making us empty promises
Man 2
Just answer us and be honest with us, because I think you think we are pampoene?

Commentary Six
Leon Basson, leader of the DA in Madibeng say they are R1 billion in debt and deeply corrupt.

Leon
They are rigging tenders and changing invoices

Commentary Seven
A recent leaked audit report reveals altered invoices and fake companies that are paid for work, not done.

Leon
The original invoice was R9100 and changed to R91 000 – here again it shows an amount of R40 00 has changed to R140 000

Commentary Eight
Madibeng is where a mayor has spent R6000 on a chocolate cake, and over half a million rand on catering, cold drink and bottled water in a single year.
And the new mayor has just shelled out almost a million for a luxury car

Yet insiders told Carte Blanche there is no money for grease and oil, or the 34 new water pumps they desperately need in water and sanitation

LINK
For several weeks we filmed from the top of Brits down to this point closer to the river – in each case we found sewerage pump stations spewing their vile contents into the veld, the roads and the streams

Commentary Nine
And here our cameras bust Madibeng pumping raw sewerage straight into a channel of the Crocodile River.

Julius Kleynhans
At the end of the day something like this is criminal

Commentary ten
Afriforum have repeatedly raised the alarm about both mismanagement and the water in Madibeng. They are not alone, insiders paint a picture of a mafia style operation rather than a municipality, but most are too afraid to go on camera.

SIPHO
This municipality is going down the drain. Somebody must do something. But I can tell you in Madibeng the officials cannot say what I am saying in public.

Commentary eleven
Fixing Madibeng is the job of Municipal manager Monde Juta, suspended twice and back in his job, despite recommendations by a government task team that he face criminal charges.

Sipho
Even the ordinary councilors are saying these people were not supposed to have come back from suspension

Commentary twelve
Millions have been spent on water infrastructure yet in Hartbeespoort pipes burst all the time, and in townships water supply is unpredictable. Even when it comes down the pipes, few trust it to drink.

MAN 1
You can go to the tap. It smells bad. It’s like sewerage

Commentary thirteen
The Crocodile River is where the water for Brits and some of the nearby townships is abstracted. But what we found going into the river is revolting and possibly even lethal to human health.

Ugh!


Commentary fourteen
This is what Juanne Strydom’s palette factory looks like when it rains.

Water gurgles

The blood comes from the abattoir about 500 meters up the hill from his factory in Brits.

Juan Strydom
This sewerage overspill has been coming for the last six years

Commentary fifteen
He says he has found stomach contents from the abbatoir and effluent from the leather factory close by, thrown into the sewerage system which blocks up, forcing foul smelling water to flood across his factory floor.

Juan Strydom
We have been to the local health office in Brits after which we were referred to Mmbatho – after the second call, our calls were just ignored. Then three years after that we went to the local municipality we had an inspection here and up until now it’s been our own battle.

Commentary Sixteen
The abattoir says it’s not their fault. Madibeng don’t provide enough water or pressure and they have been trying to sort out the problem for the last four years.

LINK
Chrome is used to clean leather and Juan suspected that there might be chrome in the water. You will remember it was the subject of the Erin Brokovich movie and its carcinogenic, so we decided to test the water in this channel

Commentary Seventeen
But Brits leather deny that they are responsible for discharging chrome effluent into the river and state that their effluent is being disposed of under contract by Madibeng.

Eventually this water feeds into the Crocodile River not that far upstream from where drinking water is abstracted.


BONGANI LINK
Blood in the water blood on the streets, a bankrupt municipality….its a formidable task but the buck stops here with the premier

Commentary Eighteen
Supra Mahumapelo has a constitutional duty to ensure that municipalities in his province run efficiently

Bongani
Would you put it up there as an example of how municipalities should be run?

Premier
No it s not the best run to be honest. As we speak now we have just made an intervention through section 139 on water and sanitation. We think they are turning the corner. In the next 18 months or so they should be on the right path to being one of the best municipalities.

Commentary nineteen
But that won’t happen say our insiders until the links between a cabal of corrupt councilors and the previous Municipal Manager Phillemon Mapulane are cut.

LINK
His friends call him Philly – everyone else knows him as Mr Cash, and even though he was suspended in 2009, insiders and outsiders still blame him for Madibeng’s mess.

Josjef Moyo
No one can say no to Mr. Cash in Madibeng. Mr. Cash owns Madibeng controls Madibeng, if you say no you will be called to come and account.

Commentary twenty
Josjeph Moyo, is one of the few prepared to speak openly about Philemon Mapulane and the kickbacks he allegedly receives.

MOYO
It’s not a kickback it’s a payment to Mr Cash. Kickback might be small, but I am talking about a lot of money



Bongani
What amounts are we talking about
Joseph?
I am talking about 20 – 30 % of the tender capital.

Commentary twenty-one
Philemon Mapulane in now on the ANC NEC and an MP.
He rejects all accusations, saying they stem from this anonymous letter accusing him of corruption in 2009

Mapulane
That pamphlet was the beginning of the persecution against my character

Commentary Twenty-two
He blames the late minister Sicelo Shiceka for targeting him in a political conspiracy. In this 2009 ANC report Mapulane was accused of corruption.
But Mapulane rejects that and says he turned Madibeng into a professional operation

Bongani
Would you say you discharged all your duties in a way that was above
reproach?

Mapulane
I believe so. One thing I know we did very well was to spend all the funds allocated in terms of the Municipal infrastructure grant.

Commentary Twenty- three
Mapulane doled out the tenders- these high mast lights, cost: R76 million rand. Yet ninety of them have never been connected to the grid.

Mapulane
Well it is the responsibility of the officials to connect them

Commentary Twenty-four
The Letlhabile bus route, a 5.6 kilometre road: cost R28 million- R17.8 million over budget.

Mapulane
I can’t estimate the value of the project but I can tell you its one of the best


Commentary Twenty –five
Or the Brits substation where R20 million was paid to a contractor who never did the work

Mapulane
That project was still running by the time I was suspended

Commentary Twenty- six
In 2009 Mapulane was suspended, found guilty in a disciplinary and dismissed. But later the CCMA found in his favour.

Mapulane
All ten allegations which were made against me, were all found not to have a shred of evidence -there was an onslaught against me emanating from the politicians and influenced by what was happening in our political organization

Commentary Twenty-seven
In 2010 he was arrested and charged, but when the key witness changed his story halfway through the trial the NPA withdrew the charges waiting for further evidence. The case melted away.

Mapulane
The case was so weak that even without his confession it was still going to be thrown out

Commentary Twenty- Eight
Yet independent sources insist that to this day Mapulane determines who gets what tender and who gets hired and fired in Madibeng. They also say the current Municipal Manager answers to Mapulane

Madibeng insider 2
Juta was brought in to Madibeng by Philly- All the key positions in Madibeng- Philly is the controlling guy.

Bongani to premier
There are allegations particularly around his person that even if cases are brought against them they will be withdrawn and people dare not defy them
Premier
Its not allegations its rumour
Bongani
So in your opinion is he an honest and good man
Premier
I don’t judge people
Bongani
His critics say he lives a lavish lifestyle
Premier
Why don’t they go the police do a lifestyle audit on him. .its not our responsibility.

LINK
Mapulane can’t seem to shake the cloud of suspicions that hangs over him. It probably doesn’t help that he loves big homes in luxury estates and shiny expensive cars

Commentary Twenty-nine
Both his current and his previous homes are in Hartbeespoort’s luxury estates. Mapulane says he has made his money in property over the last 7 years.

Mapulane
I have always had an interest in property

Commentary thirty
His latest home currently under construction in the Islands is 633 square meters, and his plans were approved in only five days.

Mapulane says he can account for every asset he owns.

Bongani
So you are not as wealthy as they suggest, nor as powerful as they suggest?

Mapulane
They seem to suggest I am more powerful than the president – I am not, I am just an ordinary guy who was once a municipal manager

Commentary Thirty- one
The premier says bring the evidence- and if there is wrong-doing in Madibeng he WILL act, no matter who it is.

Premier
When we have evidence I can tell you that we will be extraordinarily ruthless. One day if we can catch one of them die poppe gaan bietjie dans!



LINK JERICHO
If it ever happens, finding the missing millions of Madibeng will require tenacity from the most dedicated of investigators. One thing is certain though the money never trickled down to this forgotten corner of Madibeng called Jericho.

Commentary thirty-two
Once there was water right into Jericho’s homes

Victor
There used to be water …for the past 15 years there is nothing

Water flowed through their taps driven by a simple pump and borehole. But then Madibeng dismantled the system and built this reservoir.

Victor
This is a white elephant – it has never worked. It doesn’t work

Commentary thirty-three
In 2010 Victor Molefe, a mild mannered resident founded Makarapa

Power Jericho power!

A grass roots organization determined to do only one thing- get water flowing through the taps of Jericho again.

Victor
We have everything we have water we have reservoirs we have pipes we have meters but we don’t have running water!

Commentary thirty- four
Since 2010 Makarapa has approached Madibeng, the chief, the Human rights commission, the public protector, two premiers and the presidency

Victor
We have exhausted all avenues

Commentary thirty-five
No one listened. While tenderpreneurs hit the big time in Madibeng, people in Jericho went back to the rivers.


Victor
For many years they have been saying they are waiting for a part from Germany

Commentary thirty-six
Then it got ridiculous. Madibeng installed mandatory water meters and charged each household R150. Water meters but no water

Victor
It’s never worked
Bongani
So you paid R150, you had no choice and it’s never worked?
Victor
Its never worked!

Commentary thirty-seven
Next came the water trucks – costing R15 million a year. Trucks that the World Health Organisation says are not a safe way to transport water, and trucks that have become a hated symbol of the corruption of Madibeng

Fransina
Daai trokke is a kukspul lorries daai goed ons vreet te vuil water.

Commentary thirty-eight
And water supply is often deliberately sabotaged just so the trucks can make money.
Leon
It’s R 1.3 million per month that has been paid to tankers

Bongani
I just want to be clear you are saying to me that people had running water – they no longer have water but the same water is being given to them in tankers at R15 million a year
Leon
YES!

PREMIER
Some people see it as an opportunity to milk the state – that is why we have intervened and said we have to look at every contract.



Commentary thirty- nine
In Jericho, disgusted with the tankers, residents chased them away and began to rebuild the old borehole system their municipality had destroyed.

Bongani
Did you know what to do?
Victor
He laughs. You know what.. we just somehow figured it out

Commentary forty
Madibeng contractors had destroyed their water pipes so they collected old ones and connected those

Victor
At times we finished our work …two to three weeks we had the system running.

Commentary forty- one
They found funds for a second machine and with so much water they needed to get their old reservoir working, but not only did Madibeng refuse to help, they stopped Jericho’s project

Victor and Bongani at the water project.
We gave them the system about two times – each time it collapsed in their hands … its not going anywhere

Commentary forty-two
Then in March- at last Water Affairs promised Jericho water within 6 weeks.
Now they are told it’s going to be November. Victor is also concerned that they are being excluded from government meetings about the very project they initiated.

He says its seems the only time government responds is when people protest.

VICTOR
But the best way the government understands is riots – but if you keep writing letters they don’t hear you.

Commentary forty-three
Madibeng have been deaf to their citizens for too long. But will they hear this? The water we sampled with Afriforum contains excessive amounts of chrome. Is it the dangerous chrome 6? Our experts suggest it may be, and further investigations are necessary.

There are also high levels of arsenic, selenium and aluminium.
We have been advised the water we sampled is unsuitable for irrigation or healthy aquatic ecosystems.

THE END
18 minutes 03 seconds.


PROMO ONE 15
Over spending and excess at Madibeng municipality- said to run more like a mafia style operation than a centre of excellence.
Moyo
Mr Cash owns Madibeng. Mr Cash controls Madibeng

PROMO TWO 10 seconder
Few people trust the water in Brits.
MAN 1
It smells like sewerage
Commentary
We take some water samples and make an alarming discovery

PROMO ONE 15
Madibeng municipality left the people of Jericho without water for over a decade- tired of waiting they made their own plans
Victor
For many years they have been saying they are waiting for a part from Germany

Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 08 July 2015 Press Release: Dying for water in Madibeng The party is over in Madibeng. For years, ‘tenderpreneurs’ have drained the coffers with large, overpriced infrastructure projects - some are missing, others don’t work. Now the municipality is a billion rand in debt, with assets worth R1.5-bn missing, and they're struggling to pay Eskom and their water bills. According to reports, looting continues. The premier says they are working hard to turn around North West’s failing municipalities, but residents have grown impatient, with angry protests over water having led to several deaths. Carte Blanche goes in search of answers. Script: DYING FOR WATER FINAL SCRIPT 22 May 2015 Commentary One Last year, not far from Marikana – four people were shot dead by police. Gunshots Their crime, protesting about a lack of water GUNSHOTS This year, further water protests erupted across the North West’s Madibeng Municipality. A water affairs investigation into what happened found that there could be 100 water supply systems like Madibeng where the management has deteriorated to such an extent a water crisis could happen any day. Sammy Matubela I spend about R800 a month on water Commentary two Here clean water costs a fortune. Pensioners can no longer afford a basic human right Fransina Die helfte van my pensionare geld hou ek apart vir water Commentary Three 15 years ago Madibeng merged Hartbeespoort, Brits and the surrounding townships. Almost from the outset overpriced multimillion rand tenders were awarded. Former resident, attorney Josjeph Moyo, owns this run down bakery there. He alleges corrupt councilors still get huge kickbacks. Josjeph Moyo They want to enrich themselves but they forgot the poor people on ground. Commentary four By 2007 an investigation was handed to the Scorpions detailing 26 cases of corruption. Nothing happened. LINK There were others, one of those is sitting on the Presidents desk six years after it was commissioned. Commentary Five Now Madibeng is bankrupt. They struggle to pay water and electricity and residents both rich and poor, are venting their anger at the current budget meetings underway. Dominique We will hunt you down because you are making us empty promises Man 2 Just answer us and be honest with us, because I think you think we are pampoene? Commentary Six Leon Basson, leader of the DA in Madibeng say they are R1 billion in debt and deeply corrupt. Leon They are rigging tenders and changing invoices Commentary Seven A recent leaked audit report reveals altered invoices and fake companies that are paid for work, not done. Leon The original invoice was R9100 and changed to R91 000 – here again it shows an amount of R40 00 has changed to R140 000 Commentary Eight Madibeng is where a mayor has spent R6000 on a chocolate cake, and over half a million rand on catering, cold drink and bottled water in a single year. And the new mayor has just shelled out almost a million for a luxury car Yet insiders told Carte Blanche there is no money for grease and oil, or the 34 new water pumps they desperately need in water and sanitation LINK For several weeks we filmed from the top of Brits down to this point closer to the river – in each case we found sewerage pump stations spewing their vile contents into the veld, the roads and the streams Commentary Nine And here our cameras bust Madibeng pumping raw sewerage straight into a channel of the Crocodile River. Julius Kleynhans At the end of the day something like this is criminal Commentary ten Afriforum have repeatedly raised the alarm about both mismanagement and the water in Madibeng. They are not alone, insiders paint a picture of a mafia style operation rather than a municipality, but most are too afraid to go on camera. SIPHO This municipality is going down the drain. Somebody must do something. But I can tell you in Madibeng the officials cannot say what I am saying in public. Commentary eleven Fixing Madibeng is the job of Municipal manager Monde Juta, suspended twice and back in his job, despite recommendations by a government task team that he face criminal charges. Sipho Even the ordinary councilors are saying these people were not supposed to have come back from suspension Commentary twelve Millions have been spent on water infrastructure yet in Hartbeespoort pipes burst all the time, and in townships water supply is unpredictable. Even when it comes down the pipes, few trust it to drink. MAN 1 You can go to the tap. It smells bad. It’s like sewerage Commentary thirteen The Crocodile River is where the water for Brits and some of the nearby townships is abstracted. But what we found going into the river is revolting and possibly even lethal to human health. Ugh! Commentary fourteen This is what Juanne Strydom’s palette factory looks like when it rains. Water gurgles The blood comes from the abattoir about 500 meters up the hill from his factory in Brits. Juan Strydom This sewerage overspill has been coming for the last six years Commentary fifteen He says he has found stomach contents from the abbatoir and effluent from the leather factory close by, thrown into the sewerage system which blocks up, forcing foul smelling water to flood across his factory floor. Juan Strydom We have been to the local health office in Brits after which we were referred to Mmbatho – after the second call, our calls were just ignored. Then three years after that we went to the local municipality we had an inspection here and up until now it’s been our own battle. Commentary Sixteen The abattoir says it’s not their fault. Madibeng don’t provide enough water or pressure and they have been trying to sort out the problem for the last four years. LINK Chrome is used to clean leather and Juan suspected that there might be chrome in the water. You will remember it was the subject of the Erin Brokovich movie and its carcinogenic, so we decided to test the water in this channel Commentary Seventeen But Brits leather deny that they are responsible for discharging chrome effluent into the river and state that their effluent is being disposed of under contract by Madibeng. Eventually this water feeds into the Crocodile River not that far upstream from where drinking water is abstracted. BONGANI LINK Blood in the water blood on the streets, a bankrupt municipality….its a formidable task but the buck stops here with the premier Commentary Eighteen Supra Mahumapelo has a constitutional duty to ensure that municipalities in his province run efficiently Bongani Would you put it up there as an example of how municipalities should be run? Premier No it s not the best run to be honest. As we speak now we have just made an intervention through section 139 on water and sanitation. We think they are turning the corner. In the next 18 months or so they should be on the right path to being one of the best municipalities. Commentary nineteen But that won’t happen say our insiders until the links between a cabal of corrupt councilors and the previous Municipal Manager Phillemon Mapulane are cut. LINK His friends call him Philly – everyone else knows him as Mr Cash, and even though he was suspended in 2009, insiders and outsiders still blame him for Madibeng’s mess. Josjef Moyo No one can say no to Mr. Cash in Madibeng. Mr. Cash owns Madibeng controls Madibeng, if you say no you will be called to come and account. Commentary twenty Josjeph Moyo, is one of the few prepared to speak openly about Philemon Mapulane and the kickbacks he allegedly receives. MOYO It’s not a kickback it’s a payment to Mr Cash. Kickback might be small, but I am talking about a lot of money Bongani What amounts are we talking about Joseph? I am talking about 20 – 30 % of the tender capital. Commentary twenty-one Philemon Mapulane in now on the ANC NEC and an MP. He rejects all accusations, saying they stem from this anonymous letter accusing him of corruption in 2009 Mapulane That pamphlet was the beginning of the persecution against my character Commentary Twenty-two He blames the late minister Sicelo Shiceka for targeting him in a political conspiracy. In this 2009 ANC report Mapulane was accused of corruption. But Mapulane rejects that and says he turned Madibeng into a professional operation Bongani Would you say you discharged all your duties in a way that was above reproach? Mapulane I believe so. One thing I know we did very well was to spend all the funds allocated in terms of the Municipal infrastructure grant. Commentary Twenty- three Mapulane doled out the tenders- these high mast lights, cost: R76 million rand. Yet ninety of them have never been connected to the grid. Mapulane Well it is the responsibility of the officials to connect them Commentary Twenty-four The Letlhabile bus route, a 5.6 kilometre road: cost R28 million- R17.8 million over budget. Mapulane I can’t estimate the value of the project but I can tell you its one of the best Commentary Twenty –five Or the Brits substation where R20 million was paid to a contractor who never did the work Mapulane That project was still running by the time I was suspended Commentary Twenty- six In 2009 Mapulane was suspended, found guilty in a disciplinary and dismissed. But later the CCMA found in his favour. Mapulane All ten allegations which were made against me, were all found not to have a shred of evidence -there was an onslaught against me emanating from the politicians and influenced by what was happening in our political organization Commentary Twenty-seven In 2010 he was arrested and charged, but when the key witness changed his story halfway through the trial the NPA withdrew the charges waiting for further evidence. The case melted away. Mapulane The case was so weak that even without his confession it was still going to be thrown out Commentary Twenty- Eight Yet independent sources insist that to this day Mapulane determines who gets what tender and who gets hired and fired in Madibeng. They also say the current Municipal Manager answers to Mapulane Madibeng insider 2 Juta was brought in to Madibeng by Philly- All the key positions in Madibeng- Philly is the controlling guy. Bongani to premier There are allegations particularly around his person that even if cases are brought against them they will be withdrawn and people dare not defy them Premier Its not allegations its rumour Bongani So in your opinion is he an honest and good man Premier I don’t judge people Bongani His critics say he lives a lavish lifestyle Premier Why don’t they go the police do a lifestyle audit on him. .its not our responsibility. LINK Mapulane can’t seem to shake the cloud of suspicions that hangs over him. It probably doesn’t help that he loves big homes in luxury estates and shiny expensive cars Commentary Twenty-nine Both his current and his previous homes are in Hartbeespoort’s luxury estates. Mapulane says he has made his money in property over the last 7 years. Mapulane I have always had an interest in property Commentary thirty His latest home currently under construction in the Islands is 633 square meters, and his plans were approved in only five days. Mapulane says he can account for every asset he owns. Bongani So you are not as wealthy as they suggest, nor as powerful as they suggest? Mapulane They seem to suggest I am more powerful than the president – I am not, I am just an ordinary guy who was once a municipal manager Commentary Thirty- one The premier says bring the evidence- and if there is wrong-doing in Madibeng he WILL act, no matter who it is. Premier When we have evidence I can tell you that we will be extraordinarily ruthless. One day if we can catch one of them die poppe gaan bietjie dans! LINK JERICHO If it ever happens, finding the missing millions of Madibeng will require tenacity from the most dedicated of investigators. One thing is certain though the money never trickled down to this forgotten corner of Madibeng called Jericho. Commentary thirty-two Once there was water right into Jericho’s homes Victor There used to be water …for the past 15 years there is nothing Water flowed through their taps driven by a simple pump and borehole. But then Madibeng dismantled the system and built this reservoir. Victor This is a white elephant – it has never worked. It doesn’t work Commentary thirty-three In 2010 Victor Molefe, a mild mannered resident founded Makarapa Power Jericho power! A grass roots organization determined to do only one thing- get water flowing through the taps of Jericho again. Victor We have everything we have water we have reservoirs we have pipes we have meters but we don’t have running water! Commentary thirty- four Since 2010 Makarapa has approached Madibeng, the chief, the Human rights commission, the public protector, two premiers and the presidency Victor We have exhausted all avenues Commentary thirty-five No one listened. While tenderpreneurs hit the big time in Madibeng, people in Jericho went back to the rivers. Victor For many years they have been saying they are waiting for a part from Germany Commentary thirty-six Then it got ridiculous. Madibeng installed mandatory water meters and charged each household R150. Water meters but no water Victor It’s never worked Bongani So you paid R150, you had no choice and it’s never worked? Victor Its never worked! Commentary thirty-seven Next came the water trucks – costing R15 million a year. Trucks that the World Health Organisation says are not a safe way to transport water, and trucks that have become a hated symbol of the corruption of Madibeng Fransina Daai trokke is a kukspul lorries daai goed ons vreet te vuil water. Commentary thirty-eight And water supply is often deliberately sabotaged just so the trucks can make money. Leon It’s R 1.3 million per month that has been paid to tankers Bongani I just want to be clear you are saying to me that people had running water – they no longer have water but the same water is being given to them in tankers at R15 million a year Leon YES! PREMIER Some people see it as an opportunity to milk the state – that is why we have intervened and said we have to look at every contract. Commentary thirty- nine In Jericho, disgusted with the tankers, residents chased them away and began to rebuild the old borehole system their municipality had destroyed. Bongani Did you know what to do? Victor He laughs. You know what.. we just somehow figured it out Commentary forty Madibeng contractors had destroyed their water pipes so they collected old ones and connected those Victor At times we finished our work …two to three weeks we had the system running. Commentary forty- one They found funds for a second machine and with so much water they needed to get their old reservoir working, but not only did Madibeng refuse to help, they stopped Jericho’s project Victor and Bongani at the water project. We gave them the system about two times – each time it collapsed in their hands … its not going anywhere Commentary forty-two Then in March- at last Water Affairs promised Jericho water within 6 weeks. Now they are told it’s going to be November. Victor is also concerned that they are being excluded from government meetings about the very project they initiated. He says its seems the only time government responds is when people protest. VICTOR But the best way the government understands is riots – but if you keep writing letters they don’t hear you. Commentary forty-three Madibeng have been deaf to their citizens for too long. But will they hear this? The water we sampled with Afriforum contains excessive amounts of chrome. Is it the dangerous chrome 6? Our experts suggest it may be, and further investigations are necessary. There are also high levels of arsenic, selenium and aluminium. We have been advised the water we sampled is unsuitable for irrigation or healthy aquatic ecosystems. THE END 18 minutes 03 seconds. PROMO ONE 15 Over spending and excess at Madibeng municipality- said to run more like a mafia style operation than a centre of excellence. Moyo Mr Cash owns Madibeng. Mr Cash controls Madibeng PROMO TWO 10 seconder Few people trust the water in Brits. MAN 1 It smells like sewerage Commentary We take some water samples and make an alarming discovery PROMO ONE 15 Madibeng municipality left the people of Jericho without water for over a decade- tired of waiting they made their own plans Victor For many years they have been saying they are waiting for a part from Germany Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for CRUNCH TIME IN MADIBENG (4551 ) Joy Summers 26 May 2015

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): ESKOM has threatened 8 hours of blackouts to those municipalities that dont pay it. Madibeng is one of them, but where did the money go
metadata.Further information: A month ago Chief Financial officer of Madibeng municipality, Tondy Nkuna stood up and said ENOUGH and promptly resigned. Her letter to the Municipal manager explains that since March 2014 she has been under stress and the municipality failed to attend to her problems. Tondy’s stress comes from pressure to sign off contracts she knows are not kosher, and unable to sustain the pressure, she has resigned. Madibeng is one of 24 NW municipalities that for the last eight years at least, cant get the basics right. Clean audits, clean water, functioning sewerage are rare commodities here. WATER Last month another shortage of water across Madibeng was the final straw. In bloody and violent clashes people died on the streets. In Jericho the people who once had running water had none for ten years thanks to Madibeng. But millions have been budgeted over the years to sort out the water problems. So what happened? Why is it that the only way that people who once had piped water now had to rely on water trucks – costing the council over a million rand a month and going into the pockets of contractors giving kickbacks to well placed politicians This is the land of the burst water pipe. For the last three days one of Hartebeespoort suburbs is once again without water. People are so fed up they arrived with posters at a budget meeting demanding the pipes be fixed. The Sewerage situation is no different. An insider says told Carte Blanche they don’t have money for grease or pumps. He has listed about 28 pumps that are desperately needed here. In the meantime the council pumps raw sewerage into the crocodile River and abstracts source water for drinking water a couple of hundred meters downstream. If that is not enough the abbatoir releases blood into the sewers that run into a stream that runs into the Crocodile River. The leather tanning factory uses chrome to clean its leather and that too makes its way into Brits drinking water. Councillors say the water is fine to drink but receipts show just how much they spend on bottled water, and cold drinks. And there are thousands of rands spent on VIP toilets – but the chemicals are so strong says one angry resident they burn our butts. At the budget meeting he warned that “ you councilors who steal the money – we will hunt you down. People are angry. Its crunch time here Yet go through the figures, the asset registers and a picture emerges of ANC councilors spending fortunes on events, parties, transport, cars… Below are a few of the items Two telephone poles – worth about R3000 max – paid over a R1 million rand R948 000 rand for the new mayors car R45 000 a month lease for the previous mayors car R6000 for the previous mayors chocolate cake And hundreds of thousands on VIP toilets, catering, PA systems and events Everyone knows who is behind the theft but few have proof and those that do have given up trying to catch them. At least nine years of investigations mysteriously go nowhere as criminal charges seem to disappear in a whiff of smoke. Mr Cash, the former Municipal manager has built his empire in the municipality, says a source and entrenched it in waste management. Mr Cash AKA Philemon Mapulane was suspended in 2009 on charges of fraud and corruption. He was arrested but all charges against him were withdrawn. He is currently building his fourth or fifth home- at a cool R11 million, not bad for a man who started off as a meter reader. When he was suspended for corruption in Madibeng, he was promoted to treasurer in the North West Province. Now he sits on the NEC of the ANC and is a member of parliament. Two weeks ago there were more suspensions by the current municipal manager Mr Mondi Juta. Why he is back is anyone’s guess because a 2013 report recommended criminal charges against him too. LETS STOP THE CROOKS IN THE MUNICIPALITY These were the words of DA councilor Eddie Barlow this morning who told a portfolio committee that they need an administrator in every department as the only way to stop the rot. The portfolio committee will write a report and submit it to the minister who has 14 days to decide what to do. With over a billion rand in debt Madibeng is effectively bankrupt – and they spend more than their current revenue. They are hoping to meet Eskom on the 3rd May and come to an arrangement where they can pay R50 million and the other R20 million in tranches. MORE TO COME
